Steinem made the personal political: An illegal abortion at 22 preceded decades of fighting first to legalize abortion and then to defend that right. Steinem died peacefully, surrounded by people who loved her at her home in New York City, according to a Thursday announcement posted from her and her foundation's Instagram accounts. "Gloria's greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard," the announcement said. Flashback: Steinem first drew national attention as a journalist in 1963 when she went undercover as a Playboy Bunny and exposed the job's low pay and sexist treatment. Privately, she was a workhorse: someone who hid behind her accessories, felt she’d come to the women’s movement late (in her mid-30s), and spent much of the rest of her life hustling to make up for it. If these two identities came into conflict—the persona and the person, the superstar feminist who was terrified of public speaking—Steinem, who died yesterday at the age of 92, simply pushed on. Her politics and her life both revolved around her steadfast commitment to the idea that all women are human beings deserving of equal opportunity, and that uniting around this concept could change the world. articles.summary: Glowing obituaries are pouring in after the death of feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who was born in 1934. The Associated Press called her “a potent voice of US feminism,” and the Washington Post heralded her as the “lodestar of the modern women’s movement.” It is hard to overstate her influence upon Western women. Gloria Steinem wasn’t just one among many feminists; she was the “it” girl who normalized feminism and made it broadly attractive. Prior to her arrival on the scene, the movement was populated by angry, cantankerous, and mentally ill women whose irascibility made them difficult to work with: Kate Millett was mentally ill and an “out” bisexual; Angela Davis was an angry Black Panther; and Betty Friedan wasn’t the kind of woman other women dreamed of being like. And then came Gloria. Her long blond tresses, aviator glasses, and lithe physique opened the door to a new chapter for feminism. She was articulate, savvy, and a fresh force for the feminist movement. Not everyone appreciated the star power she brought to the movement. That is why the Trump administration is preparing to revoke the visitor visas of up to 200,000 foreign nationals who later sought asylum. articles.summary: The true language of an AI model is math — or in tech lingo, matrix multiplication — but a quirk of how models are built means they communicate with the outside world in English. So when OpenAI’s agents, in their hack of Hugging Face this summer, figured out a way to build a kind of message board, it looked eerily like a bunch of people speaking to each other. That’s why Dwarkesh Patel controversially referred to them as a “civilization” in a recent blog post , nicknaming individual agents after figures in ancient Macedonia and Rome. It was compelling because it was understandable. Ancient civilizations are most known for one thing: conquering. And that’s the worry. If OpenAI’s agents are Romans, humanity represents the barbarians. But Dwarkesh’s civilizations will need to be a lot more powerful to conquer the world. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he expected US envoys to hold talks in Moscow and Kyiv in coming days, suggesting Washington, which diverted its focus to the Iran conflict, is renewing efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war as both sides wage an increasingly deadly aerial campaign. Zelenskyy is also contending with domestic political turmoil involving high-profile firings , graft scandals , and strife within government agencies — discord that burst into the open Thursday after rival Ukrainian intelligence units exchanged fire on the streets of Kyiv. — Brendan Ruberry

articles.title: Why Ukraine’s drained Kakhovka Dam is strategic for Russia
articles.author: Sonya CIESNIK
articles.summary: Small groups of Russian soldiers have been inching forward through the vast, drained Kakhovka reservoir since they blew up the dam in June 2023. Russian forces are infiltrating this “no man’s land” for reconnaissance purposes rather than for a future military offensive, said a military expert.
